**Why no function's result has a sensitivity, confirmed.** The plan's
reading was likely right in its effect and needs one correction in its
mechanism. `Ad::build_vjp` seeds the reverse sweep with
`adj[result] = ct`, the `.vjp`'s last parameter, so `AdjointMap` *does*
name the result's adjoint: the `let` of the result maps to the cotangent
parameter (or, when the body also reads its result, to the `add` that
accumulates into it). But the reference interpreter records its 1-norms
per `let` only (`Interp::call`, over `func.body.lets`), never for a
function's parameters, and `sensitivity::from_run` looks for the sum at
`<f>.vjp/%<ct>`, finds none, and drops the site. So a callee's result,
whose adjoint is its `.vjp`'s `ct` argument, and the entry's, whose adjoint
is the sweep's seed, get no sensitivity, and `solve::sites()`, which keeps
the sites with both an envelope magnitude and a sensitivity, never offers
them. **Step 4** records the 1-norm of a `.vjp`'s cotangent argument as the
sweep enters it, keyed by its parameter's site, so that `from_run` reads
it; a function called from several places keeps the largest, as for any
site. The entry's own result then has the seed's 1-norm: 1 on a scalar
entry, ∂L/∂L, and the output's element count under the seed of ones a
tensor entry gets.

Seen on the tutorial's `loss` at `B = 4` (`presk dump --stage sensitivity
--sites 200`): `loss/%6`, the square the mean reads, at 1.0, and none of
`loss/%7`, the entry's result, `RMSNorm.apply/%10` and `Block.apply/%8`,
the callees' results.

**V5's baseline: 0.11.0's solved realization of the decoder natively.**
D117's realization (`presk-project/data/llama-7b-0.11.0.tar.xz`,
`llama-7b-L1_solved.json`: default `f64`, 24 stored values narrowed, every
parameter in `f64`) on `Llama.apply`, 384 tokens, by D100's protocol as
D107 ran it: the ten X925 cores pinned, ten threads, `presk plan`'s plan
under the frozen profile (45 nests stated at both batch sizes; one,
`Attention.apply/%16`, stored in `bf16`, left to the default layout, the
profile being calibrated in `f32` and `f64` only), the median
of seven calls after one warmup call, then the host by phase
(`--host-profile`, three calls timed by phase). The binary is `main`
`d784089`'s, 0.11.0's code. `experiments/pytorch_decoder.sh` gains the rows
(`REALIZATIONS="solved-0.11.0=@…" ROWS=realizations`); the run is
`out/v5-0.12.0/step0/` and a check, `step0-check/`, on 2026-10-13.

| | B = 1 | B = 20 |
|---|---|---|
| timed row: the median of seven calls in a process | 9 340 ms, the middle of five processes (7 378, 9 340, 9 362, 9 527, 9 073) | 79 758 ms (one process) |
| a call in the host profile's process | 9 383 ms (two processes: 4 790, 9 383) | 97 042 ms (one process) |
| the kernels' code, a call | 8 682 ms (4 141 in the fast process) | 94 250 ms |
| **converted at the kernels' edges** | **651 ms, 6.95 % of a call; 944 MB** (639 ms, 13.3 %, in the fast process) | **3 057 ms, 3.13 %; 4 979 MB** |
| fresh pages a call | 2.4 GB | 15.3 GB |
| all-`f32` under its plan, the same binary | 3 356 ms timed, 3 554 ms profiled, 0 converted | (D107, 0.10.1: 65 196 ms) |

So the solved realization is about 2.8 times all-`f32` at batch 1 in the
steady processes, and 1.2 times D107's all-`f32` at batch 20. Its edge
conversion is a minority of that, 7 % and 3 % of a call. Most of the
difference is the kernels' own time: under D117's realization the
products the functions return (the head, the feed-forward products, the
attention's output projection) stay in `f64`, as every parameter does, and
an `f64` kernel has half the lanes. The conversion moves the same 944 MB and 4 979
MB in every process, which are the weights its `f32` nests read, copied
from `f64` at each launch: B removes that copy and those bytes.

**Found: under this mixed realization the kernels' time varies by a factor
of two between processes.** All-`f32` does not: 3 356 and 3 554 ms here,
3 744 and 3 827 in D107. The first two processes measured, one after the
other, were fast (7 378 and 4 790 ms); the five after them took 9 073–9 527
ms. Transparent huge pages are `madvise` on falicon and the allocator does
not ask for them, so they are not the cause. The cause is not measured
here. A median of seven calls inside one process does not see this. So
V5's rows should each be timed in several processes, alternated with the
other rows. Step 5 does that, and it times 0.11.0's solved realization
again in the same session rather than reading the figure above.

## D120 — Plan 0.12.0, step 1: a parameter's storage type in the language, `params` beside `quant`; the compiler parses and checks it, and its executors take it from step 2 (2026-10-13)

**The language** (presk-specs !78, the reference at draft v0.17):
- *Chapter 4, realized types, item 3:* the parameters of an entry are
  stored in the default type, unless the record's `params` states a type
  π for the leaf, `f32` or `bf16`. A record is not a realization of the
  entry when `params` names a path that is not a leaf of its parameter
  tree, one that `quant` names too, or a type other than `f32` and `bf16`.
- *Chapter 4, realized value, item 1:* such a leaf is converted once to π
  when the entry is given it, from the value given. *Item 2:* a nest of
  any type reads it with no further rounding, since `bf16` ⊂ `f32` ⊂
  `f64` and every arithmetic type is `f32` or `f64`.
- *The paragraph after it:* the choices a realization makes are the stored
  values' types and, keyed by path, each parameter's type or quantized
  form.
- *Chapter 6:* the decision *parameter storage type* (`f32` | `bf16`, unit
  the parameter, default the program's default, changes bits) in the
  decisions table and in its own paragraph; the record's member `params`
  in the serialized form; a uniform realization types no parameter; a
  well-formed plan types or quantizes a parameter, not both.
- *Chapter 8:* W18 closed.
- A Status sentence says what compiler 0.11.0 does: every parameter in the
  default type, converted at the edge of every `f32` nest at every launch.

**`f64` is not in `params`.** The plan's decision: a parameter's own type
is narrower than a solved realization's default, and `f64` is the default's
to state. Under a default of `bf16`, `f32` is a wider type at rest, which
item 1 allows: the leaf is converted from the value given, not from its
default-typed copy.

**The compiler** (`presk-rt`):
- `Realization::params`, a `BTreeMap<String, Dtype>` beside `quant`,
  written only when it is not empty, so that no record before 0.12.0
  changes; `is_uniform` is false and `label` gains `+Nparams` when it is
  not empty.
- `Realization::check_params`: `E7001` for a type other than `f32` or
  `bf16`, for a path also quantised and, given the parameter tree, for a
  path that is not a real leaf of it, naming the paths there are, as
  `quant` does.
- It runs where the parameters are loaded, in `quantize_args` and
  `quantized_params`, which every executor's load goes through (`presk
  run`, `bench`, `serve`, the measurements of `solve` and `check
  --precision`, the C export, the launch capture of `plan` and `dump
  --stage kernel`, which take the loading path when `params` is not empty
  as they do for `quant`).
- **Until step 2, a record whose `params` passes the checks is refused
  there too** (`E7001`, "parses and checks but does not run yet"): no
  executor stores a parameter in its type yet, and a realization must
  never be run as another unnoticed. Step 2 replaces that refusal with
  the storage.
- `presk train` refuses `params` (`presk_train::refuse_params`, `E7001`),
  and so does every step `calibrate --step` and `solve --step` measure
  (`step::StepSetup::step_on`), as decided (§6, question 2): the master
  weights stay in the default type.
- `presk explain` shows the parameters' types with step 2, when a
  realization that types them can be run and listed.

**Found, for the user: a `bf16` nest reads a wider operand rounded to
`bf16`.** The reference's chapter 4 (realized value, item 2) says a nest of
storage type σ reads each operand converted to α(σ), its arithmetic type:
`f32` for a `bf16` nest. The executors convert it to σ itself. At a
launch, the host converts every input that is not in the kernel's type into
a new buffer of the kernel's type (`KernelBackend::launch`, `Buf::of`), and
a `bf16` kernel's real inputs are `bf16` buffers. So under a mixed
realization, a `bf16` nest that reads an `f32` or `f64` stored value, a
parameter of the default type or an input reads it rounded to `bf16` (twice
from `f64`, through `f32`). The C export does the same (`presk_convert`, the
manual's `export_c` table), so the three executors agree and every measured
gap is of what runs; only the definition differs. A uniform realization
is not concerned. Reading such operands as item 2 says would move the
outputs of every solved realization with a `bf16` nest that reads a wider
value, and the step table's `recipe` row (the forward and backward
functions in `bf16` reading `f32` master weights).
- *Recommended:* amend item 2 to what the kernels do, σ, then extended
  exactly to α(σ). That is what makes a `bf16` nest's traffic `bf16`'s,
  and no output moves.
- *The alternative:* make the executors read such an operand in `f32`,
  which moves those outputs (V1 would name them) and a `bf16` nest's
  traffic.
- *For `params`:* under the recommendation, a parameter stored in `f32` and
  read by a `bf16` nest is rounded to `bf16` at that nest's edge, as any
  operand. Step 2 follows the executors until the user decides. Every other
  pairing of a parameter's type with a nest's widens exactly.

**V1.** X1's harness (`out/x1/x1.sh`, 863 outputs) on this tree's binary:
no file differs from step 0's (`out/x1/step0-0.12.0`); against
`out/x1/v0.11.0`, the 22 files of D119, the generated programs' version
line and the envelopes' date. No realization of X1 has a `params` member.

**Tests:** `presk-rt/tests/params.rs` (the file form, the label, every
condition, a misspelt path naming those there are), `presk-cli/tests/
params.rs` (the conditions through `presk run` on the reference
interpreter, the kernel interpreter and the native backend),
`presk-train/tests/train.rs` (training refuses `params`).

## D121 — Plan 0.12.0, step 2: the executors store a parameter in its own type once, at load, and a kernel of a wider type widens it in its loads, with no copy at its edge (2026-10-13)

**Loading.** `Realization::quantize_args` and `quantized_params` become
`store_params` and `stored_params`: the leaves `params` types are
converted once to their types (`presk_rt::quant::typed_leaves`), the leaves
`quant` names quantised, the rest as given. A caller that realized the
arguments to the default type before quantising now calls
`Realization::realize_args`, which converts a typed leaf from the value
given, not from its default-typed copy (under a `bf16` default an `f32`
parameter keeps its bits): `presk bench`'s timed rows and host profile,
the measurements of `solve` and `check --precision --measure`, `presk
explain`'s measured section, and the native launch capture. The shapes
captures of `plan` and `dump --stage kernel` store the typed leaves of
their zeros. `presk serve` stores its weights so. Step 1's refusal is gone.

**The entry.** `KernelBackend::call` realizes its first argument leaf by
leaf with the leaf's path (`Value::map_leaves_at`): a typed parameter in
its type, shared as it is when it already is, every other leaf in the
default type as before.

**The kernels.** A new buffer kind, `BufKind::Wide(τ)`: reals of a type
narrower than the kernel's, which the kernel's loads widen exactly.
- *Where it is set.* `KernelBackend::launch` marks an input whose buffer
  is narrower than the kernel's type (`host::narrower`) as integer weights
  are marked, after lowering, and lends the buffer instead of converting
  it. The marking is part of the cache key. It happens only under a
  realization that types parameters, so that no other kernel changes.
  The launch capture keeps such an input (`kernel_input`'s `keep_narrow`),
  and `plan::lower_launch` marks it in the main kernel and in a pack's
  copy, so that `presk plan` prices the kernels the host launches
  (`cost::elem_bytes` counts τ's width).
- *The native backend.* A scalar load widens a `bf16` by its bits and an
  `f32` by `fpromote`. A vector load takes four `bf16` lanes into `f32x4`
  (`uwiden_low`, a shift) or two `f32` into `f64x2` (`fvpromote_low`), and
  any other pairing lane by lane.
- *The kernel interpreter* already loads every buffer type exactly, and is
  unchanged.
- The listing prints such an input in its own type (`%1 : bf16[4, 4]` in an
  `f32` `dot`); PSK-Kernel's definition gains the kind (presk-specs, the
  reference at v0.17).

**Not a copy, mostly.** A parameter read through a reshape (`split`,
`merge`) is copied by the host's `with_data`, which keeps `f32` and widens
`bf16` to `f64`, exactly. So a `bf16` parameter read so, as the decoder
reads its output projection, is still converted where an `f32` nest reads
the copy, with the same bits. Keeping `bf16` there changes the C export's
mirror of it, and is left.

**A `bf16` nest and an `f32` parameter** follow the executors (D120's
finding, the user's to decide): rounded to `bf16` at the nest's edge, as
every wider operand of a `bf16` nest.

**V2 holds on both executors** (`presk-cranelift/tests/params.rs`).
- *The cases:* the test set (`tests/plan/entries.txt`), the tutorial's
  `loss`, and the Llama decoder's `Llama.apply` and `loss` at tiny
  constants, every parameter typed: `f32` and `bf16` under `f64`, `bf16`
  under `f32`, `f32` under `bf16`. That makes 56 realizations.
- *Rounded once:* on the kernel interpreter and on the native backend
  alike, each gives the bits the same record without `params` gives on the
  parameters rounded to their types before the run, wherever no parameter
  is wider than the default.
- *The two executors against each other:* they agree bit for bit in the
  30 of 42 comparable cases where they already agree on the rounded
  parameters; in the other 12 their `exp` and `log` differ (D78).
- *The C program* is D122's.

**V3 as a test.** On the tutorial and the decoder at tiny constants, with
every parameter in a type no wider than the nests that read it (`bf16`
and `f32` under `f64`, `bf16` under `f32`):
- the host's conversion phase moves no byte (`HostProfile::bytes_of`,
  public for it);
- each parameter at rest is a buffer of its own type.

The decoder's figures at the 7B width are step 5's.

**`presk explain`** lists a given realization's parameters stored otherwise
than in the default type (§6.3, and the summary's count); a snapshot,
`tutorial-typed`, on `tests/plan/tutorial-typed.json` (one nest typed
apart, two parameters typed). Step 4 rewrites §6.3.

**V1.** X1 on this tree: no file differs from step 1's. `make test` and
`plan-check` pass.

## D122 — Plan 0.12.0, step 3: the C export keeps a parameter in its own type in the arena and its kernels widen it as the native ones do; C1 and C5 hold under such realizations (2026-10-13)

The C program needed no change but its kernel printer.
- *The host and the arena already follow.* The host is recorded from the
  native run (`presk-kernel/src/record.rs`), and the recorded entry
  carries each argument in its realized type. So a typed weight has its
  type in the program's `_in` struct and its arena (`const uint16_t
  *theta_blocks_proj_w`), and the `.psk.d` reader converts the file's
  reals to that type as it reads them, as it does every weight.
- *The kernel printer* gives a widened input its own C type and widens its
  loads, `presk_bf16_to_f32` or a cast to `double`, as the native backend
  does (`kernel_fn`, `wide_load`).
- *The SCoP mode* refuses a kernel with a widened input, as it refuses
  integer weights.
- `Store::of_spec` gives a widened input its type's store.

`typed_parameters_compute_the_native_backends_bits`, part of `make test`
and `make c-conformance`):

## D123 — Plan 0.12.0, step 4: the solver offers the functions' results and the parameters by path, and takes an entry whose result is a tensor under a budget on its largest gap (2026-10-13)

**The functions' results.** As D119 found, `AdjointMap` names a result's
adjoint, a `.vjp`'s cotangent argument, but the reference interpreter
recorded 1-norms per `let` only. `Interp::call` now records the 1-norm of a
`.vjp`'s argument named `ct` as it enters, at the site of that parameter,
the largest over calls as for every site; `sensitivity::from_run` finds
it. On the tutorial's `loss`: `loss/%7` 1.0 (the seed), `RMSNorm.apply/%10`
2.41, `Block.apply/%8` 1.23, where none was listed. A result whose role is
a decision (a primitive's result) is then offered like any stored value;
one carried (a call's or a fold's result) stays carried.

**The parameters, by path.** `solve::Roles` gains the parameters the
solver offers (`ParamSite`: path, elements, largest magnitude, sensitivity,
and the field sites that read it).
- *Which nests read a parameter* is followed from the entry's first
  parameter through fields, projections, calls, closures and folds
  (`solve::param_reads`): a field site of a function called on several
  subtrees reads several paths (`RMSNorm.apply`'s `θ.γ` reads
  `blocks.norm.γ` and `final.γ`), and a stacked subtree sliced by a fold
  keeps its path, as the type is every layer's.
- *Its term* is `s · u(t) · |θ|` with `t` the narrowest of its own type and
  the types of the nests that read its fields (or the default, where a
  field is read by a call, or no field reads it). The value a nest reads is
  rounded at rest and again at a narrower nest's edge, so this charges
  both, once. The field sites that read a parameter carry no term of their
  own any more: until 0.11.0 they followed their readers, and their term
  is now the parameter's. Typing a parameter `f32` where only `f32` nests
  read it adds nothing to the estimate and saves its bytes, as it changes
  no bit.
- *Its sensitivity* is the 1-norm of its leaf of the parameters' cotangent.
  This departs from the plan's question 3, which decided the sum of each
  partial's norm. The sweep returns the cotangent whole anyway, as the
  `.vjp`'s result (D105's peak holds it), so its leaves' exact 1-norms are
  read as it returns, and then it is dropped: no memory beyond what the
  sweep already took, and the exact norm rather than an upper bound. As
  decided, it is never kept beyond the sweep, but under `--quant`, as
  before.
- *Its cost* is its bytes at rest, elements × width (under `--profile`, the
  roofline's time of those bytes); the nests' costs are unchanged. So the
  traffic every ratio counts now has the weights in it, D109's "with
  weights" column.
- `--quant`'s integer types stay a pass on top of the float assignment
  (D44's), priced by the whole cotangent, now with each candidate's float
  bytes at its own type; a parameter it quantises leaves `params`. The plan
  says the integer types join the same menu. They do not: their rungs are
  priced element by element (the root-sum-square of D49), the float rungs
  by a 1-norm, and one estimate for both is a design of its own. Left, and
  said.

**An entry whose result is a tensor** (the plan's question 5, as decided):
- `presk solve --budget-abs EPS` beside `--budget` (relative to the
  output's largest magnitude), one or the other (`solve::Budget`);
- the entry must return a real tensor of any shape, an open prefix bound at
  the run included (`returns_real`); a scalar is one;
- the exact reference now runs before the sweep, to shape the seed: ones
  over the output;
- the sweep's sensitivities are divided by the output's elements, so that
  the estimate is the first-order change of a mean element, compared with
  the budget on the largest. It ranks; the measured largest elementwise gap
  decides, and the solver widens as since D41;
- the output's print says so ("on the largest elementwise gap of its N
  outputs", "of a mean output element").

*Found:* where the output's elements sum to a constant, as a layer norm's
do, the seed of ones ranks nothing. On `LayerNorm{8}.apply` every
sensitivity is about 10⁻⁴⁰, and the solver reaches the budget by seven
widening rounds from a proposal that narrowed everything. That is the case
the decided fallback, random-sign probes, is for. The course GPT's logits
do not sum to a constant; V6 says whether they widen much.

**The bound** charges the parameter tree at the narrowest of the default
and the types `params` gives its leaves (`propagate`: the tree is one
bound, the join of its leaves).

**`presk explain`, §6.3.** With a solve, the parameters are decisions in
the breakdown, by path, their term in the estimate; the prose says how. With
a realization given, the section lists every value the program stores with
the type the record gives it, its function's, or the default's (the
decoder's `RMSNorm.apply/%2` at 0.11.0 is no longer left out), then the
sites the record types that store nothing, then every parameter with its
type (`params`, `quant` or the default). The snapshot `tutorial-typed`
leaves ten stored values and two parameters at the default.

**Tests:** `presk-driver/tests/driver.rs` (`parameter_reads_of_the_tutorial`;
the breakdown sums to the estimate with the parameters among the
decisions); `presk-cli/tests/solve_tensor.rs`, which replaces
`solve_scalar.rs`: a tensor entry solved under both budgets, and the two
flags exclusive.

**V1.** X1 against steps 2–3: 20 files differ, all by design.
- *Solves:* every solve's print and record (the tutorial's, with and
  without `--quant`; the course GPT's at small constants).
- *Downstream of a solved record:* the bounds and kernel listings under
  them, the C export of the tutorial's, `presk quantize` on the quantised
  one.
- *The two sensitivity listings,* which gain the results' lines; the
  course GPT's 30-site listing loses four zero sensitivities at its tail,
  past the cut.
- *`err-solve-nonscalar`,* the layer norm's module entry, which is now
  solved and not refused.

No other file moves.

**The decoder's memory gate** (`out/llama_gate-0.12.0/gate.sh`, as D105's
step 4): the one-block solve at the 7B width on 16 tokens, on D105's
gate's envelope, in a 108 GB scope, alone:
- **49 min 46 s and 71.2 GB at its peak**, D105's 50 min 43 s and 71.2 GB.
  So the exact reference before the sweep, the results' 1-norms and the
  parameters' leaf norms cost no memory, and the decoder's solve at 384
  tokens should fit in its 105 GB scope as 0.11.0's did (71.7 GB, D117).
- **What it solves:** 31 of 32 stored values narrowed, the results among
  them (the head, `Llama.apply/%14`; the output projection; SiLU's
  product), and all 13 parameters in `f32` (none in `bf16`).
- **Traffic:** 2.00× less than all-`f64` with the weights counted. D105's
  solve on the same tokens was 1.65× without them, and D106's at 384
  tokens 1.05× with them (D109).
- **Gap:** measured 1.17·10⁻⁵ against 1.09·10⁻², no widening round.

### V5: speed

The decoder block's forward pass, `Llama.apply` at the 7B width and 384
tokens, natively by D100's protocol (`experiments/pytorch_decoder.sh`
with `ROWS=realizations`: the ten X925 cores pinned, ten threads, the
median of seven calls after one warmup, under `presk plan`'s plan for
each realization with the frozen profile), then the host by phase in a
process of its own. Four rows: all-`f64`, all-`f32`, 0.11.0's solved
realization (D117's) and 0.12.0's (the decoder's solve above). Each row
in several processes, as D119 found the time varying between them: three
rounds at batch 1, one at batch 20, alone on the machine, from 04:21 to
06:46 on 2026-10-15 (`out/v5-0.12.0/`).

| realization | B = 1, rounds 1 / 2 / 3 (ms) | ÷ all-`f32`, by round | B = 20 (ms) | ÷ all-`f32` | converted at edges, a call (B = 1 / 20) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all-`f64` | 7 022.7 / 8 919.1 / 8 873.5 | 2.88 / 2.30 / 2.32 | 105 662.4 | 1.56 | 0 |
| all-`f32` | 2 438.9 / 3 879.5 / 3 825.4 | 1 | 67 553.6 | 1 | 0 |
| 0.11.0's solved | 9 713.6 / 9 670.1 / 9 800.2 | 3.98 / 2.49 / 2.56 | 108 394.3 | 1.60 | 944 MB, 7.3–7.9 % / 4 979 MB, 2.7 % |
| **0.12.0's solved** | **2 441.4 / 2 798.4 / 2 524.0** | **1.00 / 0.72 / 0.66** | **46 631.2** | **0.69** | 18.9 MB, 0.3 % / 378 MB, 0.8 % |

- **The verdict at batch 1.** 0.12.0's solved realization is no slower
  than all-`f32` in any round: 1.001 at worst, within the 5 % asked.
  **V5 holds.**
- **Against 0.11.0's solved realization,** 3.5 to 4.0 times faster at
  batch 1 and 2.3 times at batch 20. 0.11.0's was 2.5 to 4 times slower
  than all-`f32` (D119: 2.78 in step 0's check).
- **Why it is faster: the results and the weights.**
  - *The results.* Under 0.11.0's realization, the functions' results stay
    in `f64`: the head, the attention's output projection, which is two
    thirds of the kernels' time under the `f32` plan (D107), and the
    feed-forward product. So its kernels take 8.8 s of a 9.5 s call (round
    1's host profile), about all-`f64`'s 9.2 s. Under 0.12.0's, they are
    `f32`, and the kernels take 2.4 s.
  - *The weights.* Under 0.11.0's realization, every parameter is stored
    in `f64`, and each `f32` nest converts the weights it reads at its
    edge: 944 MB and 0.7 s a call. Under 0.12.0's, every parameter is
    stored in `f32` and read in place: 7 ms a call converted.
- **What is still converted** is no parameter (V3 at the 7B width). The
  18.9 MB a call is the residual stream, `f32`, widened three times a
  call for RMSNorm's square, the one stored value left in `f64`:
  3 × 384 × 4 096 × 4 bytes = 18.87 MB; at batch 20, 377.5 MB. The
  parameters at rest are 1.86·10⁹ bytes, 1.74 GB of 2³⁰ bytes against
  3.47 GB in `f64`, V3's figures.
- **The plans** are all-`f32`'s but for one nest. 21 of its 22 layouts
  are the same. The 22nd is the head width's square root, one element,
  which the solved realization types `bf16` and plans no layout for.
  Both calls make 34 launches.
- **At batch 20,** one process each: 0.69 of all-`f32`. 0.11.0's row took
  108.4 s here and 79.8 s in step 0, the variance D119 found.
- **Five more processes each, after the protocol** (`out/v5-0.12.0/b1-extra/`,
  06:48 to 07:01, alternated, round 1's plans, the same commands): all-`f32`
  3 819.5, 3 870.5, 3 797.8, 3 749.1, 3 759.4 ms; the solved realization
  2 451.6, 2 461.2, 2 624.6, 2 906.7, 2 718.2 ms.
  - *Over the eight processes of each row,* the medians are 3 809 ms and
    2 574 ms, 0.68.
  - *The fastest of each* are the same: 2 439 ms and 2 441 ms, 1.001.
- **Below all-`f32` is not the types.** The two calls launch the same
  kernels under the same layouts, in the same types but for one stored
  value in `f64` and three scalars in `bf16`. And in one process of eight
  all-`f32` ran as fast as the solved realization does.
  - *All-`f32`, in 7 of its 8 processes and its 3 host profiles,* takes
    3.7 to 3.9 s. That is D107's 3 744 ms, whose kernels timed one by one
    added up to 2 470 ms: under all-`f32`, a launch inside the call takes
    longer than alone.
  - *The solved realization, in all 11 of its processes,* takes 2.4 to
    3.0 s, near that sum. Its kernels take 2.4 to 3.0 s of the call too.
  - *Neither has page faults to speak of:* all-`f32` none a call, the
    solved realization 4 608, its 18.9 MB converted.
  - *So the cause is not found.* A guess, untested: where the allocator
    places the buffers, which the solved realization's `f64` square and
    its conversions shift. Telling it needs the launches timed inside the
    call, which the host profile does not do. That is for later, not
    0.12.0: V5 asks for no slower, and it is no slower by every measure.
- **So the claim is "as fast as all-`f32`",** not "faster than it". It is
  3.5 to 4 times faster than 0.11.0's solved realization, at the same
  budget and a gap of the same order.

## D126 — After 0.12.0, the user's three decisions: a parameter's sensitivity is its leaf's exact 1-norm; `--quant` stays a pass on top, one menu a design for later; every timing of record runs each row in several processes (2026-10-15)

After the tag `v0.12.0`, the user decided the three points D123 and D124
left, each as recommended.

**1. A parameter's sensitivity is the exact 1-norm of its leaf of the
cotangent** (D123's first departure, kept).
- *What plan 0.12.0 decided* (its question 3): the 1-norm of each read's
  partial, summed during the sweep, without keeping the cotangent whole.
  That is an upper bound.
- *What runs:* the sweep returns the parameters' cotangent whole anyway,
  as the `.vjp`'s result, so each leaf's exact 1-norm is read as it
  returns, then dropped. It costs no memory: the decoder's solve peaked at
  71.7 GB, as at 0.11.0. It ranks better than the bound, most for a
  parameter read in several places (a stacked layer's, a norm's γ).
- *When to revisit:* if a sweep stops holding the cotangent whole, by
  streaming it, the summed partials are the fallback.

**2. `--quant` stays a pass on top of the float assignment** (D123's
second departure, kept).
- *What plan 0.12.0 asked:* the integer types in the same menu as `f32` and
  `bf16`.
- *Why not:* the float rungs are priced by a bound per element times a
  1-norm, the integer rungs by the root-sum-square of known moves (D49).
  In one knapsack the order would follow the units, not the moves.
- *For later:* the design of one menu, both kinds of rung as a
  root-sum-square of first-order moves, is `docs/precision-menu-roadmap.md`.

**3. Every timing of record runs each row in several processes** (D119's
and D124's finding, adopted as the protocol).
- *The finding:* a call of the same plan runs in one of two modes, chosen
  per process and kept for its life. All-`f32` on the decoder block took
  3.7–3.9 s in 7 of 8 processes and 2.44 s in one; 0.11.0's solved
  realization 7.4 s in one process and 9.3 s in another (D119).
- *The protocol from now on:* D100's (the ten X925 cores pinned, the
  median of seven calls after a warmup, under the plan), with each row
  timed in several processes, at least three. The report gives the median
  across the processes' medians and the fastest, as V5 did (D124). A
  comparison between rows reads the medians; the fastest says what the
  code can do.
- *What it moves:* D107's 13.6× against PyTorch at batch 1 (3 744 ms
  against 275 ms) is one all-`f32` process, in the slow mode. Against V5's
  eight all-`f32` processes, with 0.12.0's binary, the median (3 809 ms)
  gives 13.9× and the fastest (2 439 ms) 8.9×. PyTorch's side was not timed
  again. The paper's session is told which figure is which; D107's row is
  not re-measured here.
- *The cause:* not found. A per-launch timer inside a call would name it;
  that is a diagnostic for later, in `docs/kernels-roadmap.md` ("A launch
  inside a call slower than alone").

No code changes. The experiment scripts time one process per row;
`pytorch_decoder.sh`'s output directory per run lets a timing of record
repeat rows in rounds, as V5's did (`out/v5-0.12.0/b1-round1` … `3`).

## D128 — Where the measurement changes the solver's decision: an unshifted softmax, the two-pass standard deviation and a sum of equal terms make it widen, each beside a form that does not; the widening reaches the misjudged value last; a tensor first argument no longer offered as a parameter (2026-10-16)

Every solve of record was accepted as proposed (D124: zero rounds, the
gap 700 times inside its budget). The paper's session asked for one
program on which the measurement refuses the proposal and widening lands
the realization (presk-project `docs/prompt-paper-results-2026-10-16.md`,
run 1). The record is `docs/widening-2026-10-16.md`; the tables are
`experiments/widening.sh`'s (`make widening`), on the six entries of
`experiments/widening.psk`, at seven budgets from 10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁶.

**First, a defect, fixed.** Since 0.12.0 the solver offered an entry's
first argument as the parameter of path `` when it was a tensor and not a
parameter tree. No executor runs such an argument in its own type
(`Realization::store_params` refuses it), so every proposal narrowing it
measured ∞, and the solver widened everything else back first: on the
one-pass standard deviation at 8 rows and 10⁻¹, six rounds and all-`f64`,
against no round and 1.99× with the fix. `param_sites` now offers nothing
when the first argument is not a record (test
`a_tensor_first_argument_is_no_parameter`). Every solve of record takes
its parameters first and is untouched.

**Three cases, each a thing a first-order estimate cannot see.** The
solver's estimate charges each stored value one rounding at its envelope
magnitude, weighted by its cotangent's 1-norm.

| program | estimate proposes | measured | widening | the form beside it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attn_raw`, an unshifted softmax of logits near 84 (8 rows), 10⁻³ | `f32` for four values, 6.3·10⁻⁶ against 3.7·10⁻⁴ | 0.372, the row's sum of `exp` (3.78·10³⁸) past `f32`'s range | 4 rounds, all-`f64`, 1.4·10⁻¹⁵ | the `softmax` primitive: no round, 2.00×, 4.6·10⁻⁷ |
| `std_two_pass`, rows offset to 1 000 (64 rows), 10⁻³ | `bf16` for the mean μ, whose cotangent is 4·10⁻⁴⁰ (Σ(z − μ) = 0), 4.8·10⁻⁵ against 1.2·10⁻³ | 4.3·10⁻², (δμ)²/2σ, of second order | 5 rounds, μ last, 1.00×, 4.3·10⁻⁸ | the one-pass E[z²] − μ²: no round below 10⁻¹ (its cancellation is charged at E[z²]'s magnitude) |
| `clock`, a sum of 4 096 equal terms (4 rows), 10⁻⁵ | `f32` for the sum, 7.3·10⁻⁵ against 4.1·10⁻³ | 1.6·10⁻², 650 single roundings: correlated | 1 round, the sum in `f64`, 2.00×, 6.1·10⁻⁶ | the terms with noise: no round |

**The bounds.** Under one type everywhere:
- *Overflow:* on `attn_raw` in `f32` every rule, the three bounds
  included, is below the measured gap, by 4·10⁴ to 10⁵. They are
  first-order and nothing in them compares a magnitude with the type's
  range.
- *Correlated roundings:* on `clock` in `f32`, `rss` is 10× below the gap
  and `cond` 6.4× above it; with noise in the terms, `rss` is 3.4× above.
- *The variance:* `rss` held on both forms in `f32` (2.3× and 6.8× above
  the gap) and fell to 0.68× on the two-pass form in `bf16`.

So `rss`'s independence fails where the roundings are correlated, as the
prompt expected, but not on the one-pass variance it proposed for it. On
the proposals the measurement refused, `cond` is above the measured gap and
the budget for the two-pass deviation (1.15 against 4.3·10⁻²) and the equal
terms (0.100 against 1.6·10⁻²): there the first-order estimate misjudged,
not the bound, which the solver does not verify by since it is vacuous on
a transformer (D39). Under the overflow the bound fails too.

**The widening reaches the culprit last.** It widens the value with the
largest term of the estimate, and a value the estimate misjudged has a
small one. So every innocent value goes back to `f64` first, and none is
narrowed again: `attn_raw` ends at 1.00× where the sum and its reader alone
in `f64` hold the budget at 1.33×, and `std_two_pass` at 1.00× where μ
alone in `f32` holds it at 2.00× (6.1·10⁻⁶). On `clock` the culprit is the
largest term, and the one round keeps 2.00×.

**Found and left:**
- the range is unchecked: a type that cannot hold a value's envelope
  magnitude could be refused before measuring, or the bound printed as ∞;
- the widening order is the estimate's: widening by the measured effect,
  or narrowing again after a widening holds, would find the culprit;
- a measured ∞ is either a refused run or outputs that are not finite
  (`gap::leaf_gap`), which the solver's log does not tell apart.

The outputs are archived as presk-project `data/widening-0.12.0.tar.xz`.

## D130 — PyTorch's own gap to the exact model: its float32 run of the course GPT at D = 64 is 2.95·10⁻⁶ from the exact logits on the 461 held-out windows, flips no decision and lies 158 times inside ε*(10⁻³); as close as the compiler's all-f32 (3.12·10⁻⁶); a number PyTorch can approximate by its float64 run but not certify (2026-10-16)

The paper's session asked for the competitor's run measured against the
exact reference (presk-project `docs/prompt-paper-results-2026-10-16.md`,
run 3). The record is `docs/pytorch-gap-2026-10-16.md`; the tables are
`experiments/pytorch_gap.sh`'s (`make pytorch-gap`).

**How.** `make margins` taken again (its D = 64 outputs had been removed)
with D124's curve realization at 10⁻³ and V6's added: its figures are
D125's and V6's to every digit. The course GPT at D = 64 exported to
PyTorch (`--mode readable --train`) and run by PyTorch 2.14.0 eager in
eval mode on presk's checkpoint and the same 461 windows; each position's
largest gap, argmax (the reference's) and sum written as `make margins`
writes a realization's, so that `experiments/margins.py report` counts
PyTorch's flips and bound beside the compiler's rows.

| run | largest gap | flips | bound #{m < 2ε} | inside ε*(10⁻³) = 4.67·10⁻⁴ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PyTorch `float32`, ten X925 threads | 2.948·10⁻⁶ (5.7·10⁻⁷ relative) | 0 | 0 | 158× |
| PyTorch `float32`, one thread | the same, bit for bit | 0 | 0 | 158× |
| PyTorch `float64`, ten threads | 5.878·10⁻¹⁵ | 0 | 0 | — |
| presk all-`f32` | 3.115·10⁻⁶ | 0 | 0 | 150× |
| presk solved on the logits (V6) | 7.525·10⁻⁵ | 0 | 18 | 6.2× |

**What it says.** PyTorch's `float32` run of this model is as close to its
function as the compiler's own all-`f32` and decides as the exact model
does at every position. Its `float64` run is as close to the exact logits
as presk's native `f64` (5.9·10⁻¹⁵), so the export computes the function
the source denotes. PyTorch could approximate its `float32` gap by its own
`float64` run, to 6·10⁻¹⁵; what it cannot do without an exact reference is
know that its `float64` is that close. The products go through OpenBLAS and
the rest through ATen's kernels in their libraries' orders, against the
compiler's declared order; the 6 % between the two `f32` gaps is attributed
to none of them.

Run 2's trained model at the course constants gets the same rows from the
same script (`CONSTS=`, `W=`, `MARGINS=`) with its exact logits (D129).
The outputs are archived as presk-project `data/pytorch-gap-0.12.0.tar.xz`.

## D129 — The course GPT trained at its course constants and taken through the margins: validation loss 2.3307, accuracy 0.3037, ε*(10⁻³) = 4.96·10⁻⁴; the curve's realization at 10⁻³ (1.98×, eight parameters in bf16) and the one solved on the logits (1.97×) flip none of 118 016 decisions; statement S holds at course scale; PyTorch float32 6.4·10⁻⁶ from the exact logits, the compiler's all-f32 1.8·10⁻⁵ (2026-10-16)

The paper's largest limitation was two models at their initialization and
no accuracy; at course scale nothing was trained (D93's probes are one
and a few steps). The paper's session asked for the course GPT trained
there and taken through the margins (presk-project
`docs/prompt-paper-results-2026-10-16.md`, run 2). The record is
`docs/margins-course-2026-10-16.md`.

**How.**
- *The training:* 600 steps natively in `f64` at D = 384, H = 6, L = 6
  (10.8 M parameters), on 90 % of the Code civil, B = 16, T = 256, as
  `curve.sh` trains the D = 64 model; 4 h 03 min, 24.45 s a step.
- *The curve:* `experiments/curve_course.sh`, a copy of `curve.sh`'s
  solver columns at the course constants on the trained weights, the
  envelope in 25 min and seven solves of 43 to 69 min side by side.
- *The exact logits:* `experiments/margins_course.sh`, a copy of
  `margins.sh`, at 128 bits on the 461 held-out windows in 116 chunks of
  4, twelve at a time, 2 h 28 min (180 s a window); every chunk's JSON
  kept without the parameter tree `presk run --json` prints with it (623
  MB a chunk); regrouped by 32 windows for the native rows
  (`experiments/margins_rechunk.py`), byte for byte.
- *The budget on the logits:* V6's protocol, the envelope on 4 windows
  (51 min), `presk solve --budget-abs 4.96e-4` (1 h 36 min, 3.1 GB).
- *The validation losses:* natively on every window
  (`experiments/val_loss.sh`), the exact model's from the exact logits
  (`experiments/margins_loss.py`).

**The model.** Exact validation loss 2.330740 on the 461 windows (native
`f64` within 3·10⁻¹²); accuracy 0.303722, against D = 64's 0.242442.

**The margins.** ε\*(10⁻²) = 5.04·10⁻³, **ε\*(10⁻³) = 4.96·10⁻⁴**,
ε\*(10⁻⁴) = 3.10·10⁻⁵ (Clopper–Pearson, α = 0.05; D = 64's ε\*(10⁻³) is
4.67·10⁻⁴); each half of the windows certifies the other.

| realization | gap on the logits | flips | bound | certified at 10⁻³ | validation loss − exact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all-`f32` | 1.76·10⁻⁵ | 0 | 2 | yes | −1.2·10⁻⁵ |
| the curve at 10⁻³ (1.98×; 8 parameters and LayerNorm's ε in `bf16`) | 2.82·10⁻⁴ | 0 | 52 | yes | −1.2·10⁻⁵ |
| solved at ε\* on the logits (1.97×) | 2.09·10⁻⁴ | 0 | 37 | yes | −1.8·10⁻⁷ |
| the curve at 10⁻² | 6.08·10⁻³ | 3 | 1 364 | no | −1.8·10⁻⁵ |
| all-`bf16` | 0.210 | 662 | 58 508 | no | −2.6·10⁻³ |
| PyTorch `float32` | 6.42·10⁻⁶ | 0 | 0 | yes | — |

**Statement S holds at course scale.**
- Every curve realization certified at 10⁻³ (10⁻³ to 10⁻⁷) flips none
  of the 118 016 decisions; every row's flips stay under its bound.
- ε\*(10⁻³) licenses a realization narrower than `f32`: the curve's at
  10⁻³, eight of its 21 parameters (the biases and the norms' β) and
  LayerNorm's ε in `bf16`.
- The realization solved on the logits measured 4.34·10⁻⁵ on its four
  envelope windows and 2.09·10⁻⁴ on all 461 (4.8 times, D = 64's ratio
  2.3), still 2.4 times inside ε\*.
- No solve widened, at any budget.
- The validation losses of the certified realizations are the exact
  model's to within 2·10⁻⁵, the reduction of the loss itself in the
  realization's type dominating that difference.

**PyTorch at course scale.** D130's script at the course constants:
PyTorch's `float32` run is 6.42·10⁻⁶ from the exact logits, 2.7 times
closer than the compiler's all-`f32` (1.755·10⁻⁵; at D = 64 the two were
within 6 %), no flip, the same on one thread and ten; its `float64`
1.6·10⁻¹⁴. The factor is attributed to no one difference: PyTorch's
libraries' orders against the compiler's declared sequential sums, the
longest of 1 536 terms here.

The outputs are archived as presk-project `data/margins-course-0.12.0.tar.xz`.

## D131 — A contraction's bound proved in Gappa: dot of [8, K]·[K, 8] in f32 at K = 8 to 128; under the sequential order Gappa's proof stays 2.6 to 3.1 times the compiler's cond, flat over a sixteenfold length; 3.3 to 6.0 times under interleaved(n); every proof checks, proved and cond above the measured gap everywhere (2026-10-16)

D108 proved the layer norm's bound, elementwise operations and one sum;
the paper's session asked for the shape that dominates a network, a sum
of products under the realization's declared order (presk-project
`docs/prompt-paper-results-2026-10-16.md`, run 4). The record is
`docs/gappa-dot-2026-10-16.md`; every file is under `docs/gappa-dot/`.

**How.**
- `experiments/gappa_dot.psk`: `dot` with its operands through an exact
  `+ 0` site each, so that the envelope records their magnitudes; its
  kernel is the bare product's (checked at every width and order).
- `experiments/gappa_dot.py`: a second generator, one output element with
  one rounding per operation in the kernel's order (sequential, or n
  partial accumulators over k ≡ t (mod n) added left to right); the
  hypotheses the operands' magnitudes, and with `sites` the output's.
- `experiments/gappa_dot.sh` (`make gappa-dot`): `gappa.sh`'s procedure,
  the query then the proof; K = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 under the sequential
  order and interleaved(4, 8, 16).
- Gappa 1.6.0, D108's version, built from its source release on falicon
  (no package installed; D108 ran on x86-64) with Boost 1.83's headers and
  `gmp-mpfr-sys`'s GMP and MPFR; it gives D108's largest bound on D108's
  files to the bit.

| K | proved ÷ `cond`, sequential | interleaved(4, 8, 16) | `cond` ÷ measured, sequential | proved, sequential |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 2.59× | 3.28× | 13× | 1.80·10⁻⁵ |
| 16 | 2.94× | 4.42×, 3.70× | 14× | 5.78·10⁻⁵ |
| 32 | 2.90× | 4.88×, 4.37×, 3.47× | 35× | 1.88·10⁻⁴ |
| 64 | 2.85× | 5.18×, 4.78×, 4.03× | 45× | 6.62·10⁻⁴ |
| 128 | 3.14× | 5.97×, 5.70×, 5.02× | 164× | 2.59·10⁻³ |

**What it says.**
- Gappa's bound does not open up with the sum's length: it stays within
  about three times `cond` under the sequential order (D108's layer norm:
  2.5–4.8×).
- Both bounds grow as K² (×3.2–3.9 a doubling), the measured gap far
  slower, so both lose to the measurement as K grows: `cond` 164× and
  the proof 514× the gap at K = 128.
- Interleaving lowers `cond` by its count of roundings, k/n + n against
  k − 1 (5.1× at K = 128 under interleaved(8)); Gappa's proof drops
  2.8×, so its ratio to `cond` rises to about 5. Which of the two is
  slack is not examined.

**Found and left:** the envelope records no partial sum, so Gappa's
hypotheses are boxes on the operands, where `cond` reads the measured
Σ|xᵢwᵢ|; Gappa's time grows about sevenfold a doubling (423 s at
K = 128), so K = 384 would take hours and was not run; the generator
mirrors the kernel by hand, there being no Gappa export (D108).

## D133 — Version 0.13.0 opened: the pipeline view, a provenance table every stage appends to, `presk explain --format json`, the page, the math printer and the native column; two defects under `--opt` found, one to be refused (2026-10-17)

The plan is `presk-specs/implementation/presk-plan-0.13.0.md` (presk-specs
!84, open). The user asked for it on 2026-10-17: an HTML and JavaScript
view of every stage of one compilation, down to the native code. The
stages are columns, each element linked by arrows to the elements of the
previous stage it came from, to teach how Presk works and its
mathematics. The user's own remark was that the pieces of IR need "a kind

The version makes five things:

5. **The native column,** each range of a kernel's machine code mapped to

Nothing in the version is timed, and nothing in it is owed to the paper.

## D134 — The provenance table (plan 0.13.0 step 1): every element of every stage linked to what it was made from, the IRs unchanged; `presk explain` §12 read off it; `--opt` with a realization that types sites refused; three more false rows of 0.12.0's §12 found and gone (2026-10-17)

The plan's step 1, with the user's answers of 2026-10-17 on presk-specs !84
(questions 1 to 4).

**The table** (`crates/presk-provenance`, no dependency, below
`presk-core`, question 3).
- An element is `(stage, key)`. The twelve stages are in the order the
  compiler runs them, precision before the optimizer (question 2): source,
  elab, core, ad, precision, opt, fusion, layout, kernel, launch, c,
  native.
- A link is `(child, [parents], how)`, `how` one of 26 reasons grouped by
  boundary: `defined`, `instantiated`, `typed`; `lowered_fn`,
  `lowered(rule)`; `unchanged`, `gradient`, `generated(kind)`,
  `primal(kept|stored|recomputed)`, `adjoint(rule)`, `accumulate`, `zero`,
  `seed`, `plumbing`; `site(role)`, `parameter`; `rewritten(rules)`,
  `introduced`; `fused(members, stop)`, `alone(stop)`; `laid_out(point,
  points)`; `kernel(shared_by)`, `launched(count)`, `epilogue`;
  `function(lines)`; `code`.
- An element with no child at the next stage carries an end saying why:
  the optimizer removed it, the host computes it, a call's callee computes
  it, a group the call never launches.

**Each stage returns its links beside its value**, from a traced form of its
function. The existing functions keep their signatures and their outputs.
- *The lowering:* `presk_core::lower::lower_traced`. Each `let` of a source
  function or a lambda is recorded with the kind of the typed expression it
  lowered: `call`, `ein`, `index`, `+`, a builtin's name, `stack`. Its
  parent is the typed expression at its span: the typed program is keyed
  by span.
- *Differentiation:* `presk_core::ad::transform_traced`.
  - The emitter tags each `let` it makes: the forward copy as
    `primal(kept)` of the primal; the sweep's `let`s as `adjoint(rule)`
    of the primal they differentiate, `rule` its operation (`dot`,
    `softmax`, `call`, `fold`, …); the sums of two contributions as
    `accumulate`; the zeros of a parameter nothing flowed to; a `.grad`'s
    seed.
  - Pruning keeps the numbers. After the split into `.fwd` and `.bwd`,
    `g.bwd` keeps the `.vjp`'s tags by number and `g.fwd`'s `let`s are
    `primal(stored)` of `g`'s. What the split makes anew computes nothing:
    `plumbing`, of the function it serves.
- *The optimizer:* `presk_opt::optimize_traced`.
  - Each `let` written stands for its e-class, and its parents are the
    `let`s of that class.
  - `unchanged` when the class held one `let` and the term written is that
    `let` with its operands mapped; `rewritten` otherwise.
  - `introduced` for a class no `let` had, whose parents are those of the
    rewritten `let`s that read it.
  - `removed` for a `let` whose class the result does not reach.
- *Fusion:* `presk_core::fusion::plan` and `stops` on the program the
  kernels run. A nest is a group, or a primitive alone, that the call
  launches.
- *The kernels:* `KernelBackend::launch_log` (opt-in). At each launch it
  logs the kernel's place in the listing, the nest, and the `add` a
  contraction's kernel computes as its epilogue. `presk_driver::layout::
  Hosted::launched` returns it. This replaces `presk-explain`'s match of a
  kernel's printed text, which §11 keeps for `presk bench`'s kernels, those
  of another run.
- *The C:* `Exported::kernel_of` and `kernel_lines`: which `k<n>` of
  `kernels.c` each kernel of the listing is (the export deduplicates them
  by their C text), and its lines.

`presk_driver::provenance::table` puts them together for the functions the
entry reaches. `presk explain` builds it in its `run`, and
`presk_explain::provenance` returns it alone.

**Question 4: egg's explanations change an extraction, so they stay off.**
With them on, `adamw.lr` of `train_minigpt.psk` at its tiny constants is
written back as the same 21 `let`s in another order. As decided, a
rewritten `let` names the rules that applied in its function, from the
runner's iterations.

**Finding 1, refused** (question 1). `presk_driver::opt::check_sites` and
`Opt::apply_for` refuse, `E7002`, a realization whose `storage` or `accum`
names a site of a function the optimizer wrote back, or a plan that lays
one out. This holds in `run`, `train`, `serve` and `bench`, and in `presk
explain`, which also refuses `--opt` with `--budget`. The message names
each site and what the optimizer made of it: "it types `Linear.apply/%3`,
now `Linear.apply/%7`". A uniform realization runs. A function the
optimizer leaves as it was keeps its numbers, and its sites are not
refused. The C export refused `--opt` already.

**P1 holds, every difference named.**
- On the five snapshot documents, §12 over the table prints 0.12.0's rows
  byte for byte, but for one row in each of two documents: the MLP's
  `Linear.apply/%5` and MiniGPT's.
- That row was false in 0.12.0 (finding 3). The site is the `add` the
  contraction `Linear.apply/%3` takes as its epilogue, and 0.12.0 said "none:
  the host computes it", because the launch is the product's. Now: "`k2`,
  as the epilogue of `Linear.apply/%3`'s kernel: `kernel dot+add …`".
- A sixth document, the tutorial's `loss` under `--opt` in `f32`
  (`tutorial-opt`), has an "Optimizer (§5)" row per site ("`loss/%6` under a
  new number, no rule changed it": `%12`). It names the fusion and the kernel
  0.12.0 left out or denied (finding 2), and the C launch by its new site.

**Finding 4: the C name of a kernel is not always its place in the
listing.** On MiniGPT's gradient (`tests/plan/minigpt_grad.psk`, `loss_grad`),
kernels `k36` and `k60` of the listing print the same C and are one function,
`k36`. Every later kernel `k<j>` is `k<j−1>` in `kernels.c`. 0.12.0's §12
named the C function by the listing's place, so it would have been wrong
there; the table names it from the export. No snapshot has such a program.

**P2 holds** (`presk-explain/tests/provenance.rs`): no orphan, no dangling
element, no link backwards. Forwards, every `let` of the kernels' program
is in a nest or ends with a reason, every nest launches a kernel, and every
kernel is a C function. The cases:
- the eleven entries of `make plan-check`, the coverage models at `make
  coverage`'s tiny constants, and the course GPT's `loss` at D = 64, under
  the frozen profile's plan and under `--opt`: 28 tables;
- the five programs of the test set from each of their functions through
  the stages that need no entry, with and without the optimizer;
- four documents with the exact envelope and a solve.

The tables are not small: MiniGPT's gradient has 463 `let`s after
differentiation, 319 after the optimizer, 100 nests, 93 kernels and 132
launches. The course GPT's `loss` has 107 `let`s, 29 nests and 27 kernels.

The checks found two things the table had to say:
- *A residual only the precision program has.* The precision stages read
  a differentiation that keeps every fusion group, and the kernels' program
  keeps them only for a realization that can see them (D94). Under `f32`,
  `mse.fwd/%11`, a residual computed apart to keep a group, is in the first
  and not in the second. Its precision element links, through the precision
  program's own links, to the `let` of PSK-Core it copies.
- *Groups the call never launches.* These are in the lambda a `grad` was
  taken of, which the entry reaches only through a closure it never
  applies. They are not nests: their `let`s end, "a group the call never
  launches".

**P0 holds on X1's harness.** Against `out/x1/base-0.13.0`, 19 files
differ, every line the C programs' version line or their commit.
`cargo test --release --workspace` passes: 95 test binaries.

## D135 — `presk explain --format json` (plan 0.13.0 step 2): the document's facts and the provenance table as values, `explain.json` beside `explain.md` (2026-10-17)

`--format json` writes `explain.json` beside the document
(`presk-explain/src/build/json.rs`). The layout is `format` 1, and its
schema is in the manual's `explain` chapter. It holds three things.
- **The document as values.** The header and the sections are written
  block by block (prose, tables, code, notes, attachments), the same
  strings the Markdown prints. A test (`the_json_holds_the_document_and_the_table`)
  renders the Markdown again from the JSON and finds `explain.md` byte for
  byte. So every figure of the document is in the JSON, as X3 wanted every

## D137 — The printer of the denotation and the page's mathematics (plan 0.13.0 step 4): a program as the equations of the reference's chapter 3 (2026-10-17)

**The notation first.** The printer needed forms the reference did not
state: an index named by its axes, a call through a sub-module, a stack as
its recurrence, a `let` that rebinds a name. Question 6 of the plan says
the chapter is amended first. Chapter 3 gains section 3.10, "Programs as
equations" (definitions 3.37–3.39, presk-specs !85, reference draft v0.18).
It is appended at the end of the chapter, so that no section or definition
before it is renumbered. The amendment also writes `×`, as definition
den-arith does, in two equations that wrote the elementwise product `·`
(the derivative of `softmax`, `dropout`); `·` would have read as `dot`.

**The crate `presk-print-math`** (question 8) has one tree of formulas
(`m`), rendered in LaTeX (the reference's macros `\code` and `\den`) or in
Unicode, and two entries (question 5).

- *The typed program* (`typed`) walks the syntax tree with the type
  checker's tables, as the PyTorch export does. Each function becomes its
  `let`s' equations and then `⟦f⟧(x₁, …) = e`.
  - A module's parameters are written by their names, `θ.w` understood.
    A module-typed parameter is no argument.
  - An operation is written by its name (`dot x, w`, `softmax axis seq2
    s, m`), never as its lowering. The functions of analysis are written as
    analysis writes them, and an injection is not written.
  - A number is written as the source writes it (`1e-5` is `10^{-5}`).
  - A call is written `⟦path⟧(…)`. A call through a stack becomes its
    recurrence with a fresh `y`, `y₀ = x`, `y_{ℓ+1} = ⟦m.f⟧(θ.u[ℓ], y_ℓ)`.
  - An `ein` is written as its sum, at an index named by its result's axes,
    each operand at its relabeled axes. An `ein` that a non-elementwise
    operation reads becomes an equation of its own.
  - A rebound name is primed, `x' = x + …`. A λ binder may reuse a name.
- *PSK-Core after differentiation* (`core`) writes one equation per
  binding, named as `presk dump --stage core` names it. A primitive is
  written as above, an adjoint primitive by its name, a closure as `v ↦
  ⟦f⟧(z, v)`, a `fold` as its recurrence (`5 − ℓ` reversed). Each binding
  of a generated function carries what AD's links of the provenance table
  (D134) say: `primal b, kept`, `adjoint of %5 (add)`, `accumulates the
  adjoint of …`, `the cotangent 1`.

**The command** (question 7): `presk dump --stage elab|core-after-ad
--format latex|unicode`, with `--module`, `--function` and `--standalone`
(a document with the reference's macros). A form the printer does not
write is printed as its source text and named on standard error.

**Checks.**
- Snapshots of the tutorial, the attention, the three examples and the
  course GPT (LaTeX and Unicode), and of the adjoints of `tutorial/04_grad`
  and of `mse_grad`.
- A test prints all 56 programs of the repository that type at both
  entries: none has a gap.
- `make math-check` compiles the 14 standalone documents with LuaLaTeX.
- P5's listing, for the reference's author to check:
  `docs/printer-p5-2026-10-17/listing.pdf` (6 pages), with the tutorial, the
  attention, the course GPT and the adjoints of the tutorial's `grad`.
  **P5 holds**: the user checked it on 2026-10-17 ("this is chapter's
  mathematics").

**The page's mathematics (4c).** `explain.json` gains a `tex` fact:
- a function's display and each typed expression's formula on the
  elaborated program;
- each `let`'s equation on PSK-Core and the stages after it;
- a solved site's term, `e_v = ‖∂L/∂v‖₁ · u_τ · max|v|` with its numbers,
  beside the conditioned bound's error there (`bound`);
- a contraction nest's sum, `∑_{k=0}^{K−1}`, with the realization's

At the top level, `rules` holds the contributions of each derivative the

## D138 — The native column (plan 0.13.0 step 5): each kernel's machine code, every byte with the line of the kernel it compiles (2026-10-17)

**The lines.** `presk-cranelift` keeps a counter that walks the kernel's
statements in the order its printed text writes them:
- line 1, the header, holds the prologue: the buffer loads and the
  variables' first values;
- each statement's instructions carry its own line;
- a `for` holds its test and the jump into its body, and its closing brace
  holds the step and the jump back;
- an `if` holds its test, and its closing brace the jump past it;
- the kernel's last line, its closing brace, holds the return.

Each line is set with `FunctionBuilder::set_srcloc`. After
`define_function`, the compiled code gives Cranelift's ranges
(`get_srclocs_sorted`) and, by question 9, its text of the instructions
after register allocation (`Context::set_disasm`). No capstone. The bytes
are read from the JIT's finalized code, relocations applied.

**The bytes Cranelift gives no line** are listed (`given`) and taken by
the line before them; before the first range, that is the header. They
are:
- the function's prologue, saving registers, which the plan gives to the
  function itself;
- the moves the register allocator inserts;
- the branches at a block's edge.

The page shows them in italics. A constant keeps the line of the
instruction that made it. A kernel's zero is made once, at its header, so
its accumulators' zeroing shows on line 1. That is Cranelift's account,
kept as it is.

**Nothing a run compiles changes.** The lines are set and the text is
asked for only in `presk_cranelift::machine_code`, which `presk explain`
calls under `--format json|html` with the native target; a run calls
`compile` with neither. `plain_code` compiles as a run does, and the test
finds the same bytes for every kernel.

**P4 holds** (`presk-driver/tests/native.rs`). Every kernel of the entries
`make plan-check` runs was compiled: in `f64`, `f32` and `bf16`, under
`tests/plan/default.json`, and for `SelfAttention.apply` under
`tests/plan/attention.json` (tiled, in lanes, k-blocked, split, packed, a
two-pass softmax) at `D = 64`, `T = 16`. That is 1 164 kernels and
197 252 bytes. For each one:
- the ranges run in order from 0 to the code's end, none empty and none
  overlapping;
- each range's line is a line of the kernel's text;
- the bytes are those a run compiles.

Cranelift gave no line to 23 720 of those bytes (12 %): 2 816 of
prologues, 20 680 inside the code, 224 at its end.

| Page | Kernels | Bytes | Given the line before them |
|---|---|---|---|
| The tutorial's `loss` | 9 | 984 | 104 (11 %) |
| The course GPT's `loss` at `D = 64` | 26 | 9 380 | 1 132 (12 %) |
| The Llama 2 decoder block at the 7B width | 25 | 8 596 | 3 000 (35 %) |

The decoder's share comes from its 4 × 16 tiles in lanes. Sixteen vector
accumulators are zero or loaded, so every block edge copies the sixteen
registers.

**The table and the page.**

  listed kernel's code is an element `native k<j>` of the native stage,
  linked to `k<j>` by `code`.
- **The JSON.** It writes `bytes`, `hex`, `ranges`, `given` and `disasm`
  (the manual's `explain` chapter).
- **The page.** Its last column, §9 "Native code", folds under the
  kernel's function. Hovering shows each range with its line of the kernel

- **Tests.** `the_json_holds_the_machine_code` checks the JSON with the
  native target and without it.
- **The document.** `explain.md` does not print the native column, so

## D140 — Version 0.14.0 opened: the network diagram in the pipeline view, the program as boxes and arrows drawn from the provenance table (2026-10-17)

The plan is `presk-specs/implementation/presk-plan-0.14.0.md` (presk-specs
!88, open). The user ran 0.13.0's pipeline view on their machine and, on
2026-10-17, asked for a drawing of the network inside the page, to
understand the model more easily. The design note is presk-project
`docs/presk-network-diagram-2026-10-17.md`, the prompt
`docs/prompt-network-diagram-2026-10-17.md`. It is the drawing of
presk-project `docs/presk-other-export-targets-2026-09-26.md` §4
(2026-10-01), made from the pipeline view's data.

The drawing is in a second tab of the page, Network, beside Pipeline. By
default it shows:
- the printer's formulas on the boxes;
- the shapes and bytes on the arrows, coloured by their type;
- the parameter count of each box, with its stored type;
- the cost model's work W and bytes Q of each box.

A `stack{L}` is one box ×L, which opens to one layer. A box opens in place
to its own graph. A click selects the same element in the columns. The
rule that shapes it: **the diagram is a view of the provenance table, not
a second model.** Every box, node and arrow is an element of the table,
and the drawing adds positions and numbers to them.

The version makes four things:
1. **A crate, `presk-diagram`,** with no external dependency: the graph
   of a function from the table, its numbers, and a layered layout of
   every level a reader can open, nested boxes included.
2. **JSON format 2,** `explain.json` with a `network` object.
3. **The Network tab** of `explain.html`.
4. **The exports:** `network.svg`, `presk dump --stage network --format
   json|svg|tikz`, and a generated TikZ figure of the course GPT in the
   report's chapter 8.

Nothing in the version is timed, and nothing in it is owed to the paper.

## D141 — The network diagram's graph, numbers and layout (plan 0.14.0 step 1): crate `presk-diagram`, `explain.json` format 2, `network.svg`; N1 and N2 hold (2026-10-17)

Plan 0.14.0's step 1 (presk-specs !88), with the user's answers to its
three questions (D140): the launch log records the calls above each
launch, a box's element is its call, N5 at P3's bound.

**What was made.**
- **`Launched::calls`** (`presk-kernel`). While the launches are logged,
  the kernel backend keeps the calls it is inside: each call's `let`,
  `"<function>/%<let>"`, and a fold's with its iteration,
  `"<function>/%<let>[<i>]"`, the outermost first. `call_fn` pushes its
  caller's site and pops it on return; a fold sets the iteration before
  calling its body. Nothing is recorded when the log is off, and no
  output changes.
- **Crate `presk-diagram`**, no external dependency, below
  `presk-explain`:
  - `build`: the graph of the program the kernels run (the table's stage
    `ad`, or `opt` under `--opt`), each box drawn at its own call.
    - A call box per call, named by the field of the parameters it is
      given (`ln1`), its instance from their type (`LayerNorm{64}`); its
      element is the call's `let`, and it names its callee's `fn`
      element, which every instance shares.
    - A stack box per `fold` over stacked parameters (×L).
    - An operation node per fusion element of the function (a group or a
      primitive alone, read from the table's fusion stage), and a host
      node per primitive the host computes.
    - A parameter node per parameter an operation reads; the parameters a
      box is given are its port.
    - The inputs, the result, and an arrow per value, through the
      projections and tuples the host carries.
    - A scalar of literals the host computes is a hyperparameter and is
      not drawn; one a kernel computes (`sqrt(HD : ℝ)`) is a node, so
      that W and Q add up.
  - `shape`: a callee's types at its call. One PSK-Core function serves
    every instance of its module, so an arrow inside a box takes the
    callee's type under the call's dimension arguments, the open prefix
    bound to the caller's argument's leading axes. The entry's own prefix
    is the `--dim`s it does not have, as `presk run` binds it
    (`bind_run`). Differentiation copies a callee's result type into its
    caller with the callee's prefix variable (`.bwd`'s
    `%8 : (…, ℝ[..., hidden]) = call Linear.apply.bwd…`), so a caller's
    types take the bindings its callees make.
  - The numbers:
    - a box's formula is the printer's display of its callee
      (`render::aligned`, N3), with its Unicode form for the SVG;
    - an operation's formula is its root `let`'s equation, the string its
      column shows, with a contraction's sum and order;
    - an arrow's type is in the entry's dimension names and at their
      values, with its realized type and bytes; a parameter flows in its
      stored type and bytes (D121);
    - a box's parameters are its subtree of the entry's (a quantized
      leaf's integers and `f32` scales); inside a stack, a layer's;
    - a box's W and Q are `kernel_cost`'s over the launches whose calls
      begin with its own, and an operation's over its nest's launches in
      its call.
  - `layout`: layered, top to bottom. Longest-path layers, a source
    pulled down to just before its first reader, the result last; edges
    across layers pass through; barycenter ordering over eight sweeps;
    each layer's items placed near their neighbours' centre, in order.
    An opened box is its graph laid out inside it, below a header, the
    arrows into it ending at its own inputs. One layout per opening a
    reader can reach: the entry alone, then each box opened with the
    boxes it is inside. The default opening is the entry and its first
    box.
  - `json` (format 2's `network`, written by hand), `svg` (one opening,
    the formulas in Unicode), `text` (the outline the snapshots keep).
- **`presk explain`.** `explain.json` is format 2, with `network`; the
  page refuses any other. `--format json|html` also writes `network.svg`,
  the default opening. `presk_explain::network` returns the diagram with
  what it is checked against. The manual's `explain` chapter gives the
  schema.

**Departures from the plan, each with its reason.**
- *Top to bottom, not left to right* (the note's §3 put the inputs on the
  left). Left to right, a layer is as wide as its widest formula, and
  opening a box multiplies the layers. The course GPT at level 2 (`Block`
  opened) was 4 593 × 345 pt; top to bottom it is 745 × 1 697 pt, about
  half its size on an A4 page (N4, step 3).
- *A box opened folds its siblings.* Opening a box moves what is around
  it, so a layout is computed for each path of opened boxes. Opening two
  siblings at once would need a layout per combination, or a layout in
  the page, which the plan excludes.
- *`network.svg` in step 1*, not step 3: the layout could not be judged
  without drawing it. Step 3 adds `presk dump --stage network`, the TikZ
  and N4.
- *N2's comparison with the envelope* is made where the precision stages
  read the kernels' program. Under a uniform realization of a gradient,
  differentiation keeps a fusion group for the precision stages alone
  (D94), and their program is numbered differently: the MLP's
  `mse_grad.lambda0.bwd/%10` holds 72 elements in the kernels' program
  and 80 in theirs.

**Statements.**
- *N1 holds*: every node, function, member and arrow names an element of
  the table. *N2 holds*:
  - the parameters over the entry's `θ` equal `Hosted.params`' total;
  - at each site the envelope holds, the largest count of elements over
    the arrows that carry it equals the envelope's (98 arrows);
  - in every opening, the W and the Q of the nodes drawn and not opened
    sum exactly to the entry's launches';
  - every arrow's shape is known at the entry's dimensions.
- They are checked by `presk-explain`'s `tests/network.rs` on 36
  diagrams:
  - the 14 entries of `make plan-check` and the coverage models and the
    course GPT, with and without the optimizer;
  - the six snapshot documents' compilations and the MLP's gradient;
  - the course GPT in `f64`.
- Outline snapshots keep the graphs and the default opening's positions.
- On the course GPT at D = 64:
  - 125 nodes, 133 arrows, 14 openings;
  - 112 896 parameters;
  - W = 7 362 769 and Q = 3 309 664 bytes in `f64`;
  - the four `Linear{64, 64}` boxes of a block each 264 k of W per layer.
- *N0 holds at this step.*
  - X1's harness against the baseline differs in the same 19 files as at
    step 0, by their version lines.
  - The three documents' `explain.json` (the tutorial, the course GPT
    under a budget, the decoder block at the 7B width) are 7e215f1's but
    for `format`, `network` and the finding below; their `explain.md`
    but for the version line.
  - Sizes, v0.13.0's then this step's: 224 045 → 288 003 bytes,
    680 469 → 993 539 and 1 283 647 → 1 481 857. The network is 29, 125
    and 87 KB compact, as the page inlines it; the file is pretty-printed,
    a coordinate a line.

**Finding: `explain.json` under the native target is not the same from
one run to the next.** 0.13.0 step 5 (D138) reads each kernel's machine
code after the JIT links it, and a kernel that calls a `libm` function
holds that function's address, which the loader places differently in
each process. Two runs of v0.13.0 on the tutorial differ in one kernel of
nine; the bytes' `ranges`, the lines and the sizes do not. The JSON was
said to be deterministic without `--measure` (D135). Reading the bytes
before they are linked, with the relocations named, would make it so. It
changes what the native column shows, and is put to the user on this
step's merge request; N0 compares the JSON with the native code's `hex`
and `disasm` aside.

## D145 — The native code's bytes before linking: `explain.json` the same from one run to the next (plan 0.14.0, the user's answer on presk !100) (2026-10-17)

D141 found that `explain.json` under the native target differed from one
run to the next. 0.13.0's native column (D138) read each kernel's bytes
after the JIT linked them, and a kernel that calls a `libm` function holds
that function's address in a literal: on the tutorial, the 8 bytes at
128–136 of `k4`, `erff`'s address, which the loader places differently in
each process. D135 had said the JSON was deterministic without
`--measure`. The user answered the question on presk !100, 2026-10-17:
"yes", keep the bytes before linking.

- **`presk_cranelift::MachineCode`.**
  - `bytes` are now the buffer Cranelift emitted, before the JIT links it
    (`compiled_code().code_buffer()`).
  - A new field, `relocs`, gives each field the linker fills,
    `(start, end, symbol)`, from the buffer's relocations, each target
    named by the `libm` function it is (`exp`, `erff`).
  - `plain_code`, the test that the lines change no byte, keeps the same
    bytes without the lines.
- **The text of the instructions also varied**, found by running the
  course GPT twice: a kernel calling two `libm` functions declared them
  into its function in a `HashMap`'s order, so that Cranelift's text
  numbered them `userextname0` and `userextname1` either way. They are now
  declared in their names' order. The bytes do not encode that number.
- **`explain.json`** gains the native facts' `relocs`. The page
  underlines those bytes and names their function. The manual's `explain`
  chapter says so.

**Checks.**
- `presk-driver`'s `tests/native.rs` (P4) also checks that every field
  the linker writes is zero before linking and names a `libm` function:
  129 fields in the test set's 1 164 kernels.
- `presk-cli`'s `tests/explain.rs` runs `presk explain --format json` on
  the tutorial twice, in two processes, and finds the same bytes.
- By hand, two runs each give the same `explain.json`, byte for byte:
  - the tutorial under a budget;
  - the course GPT under a budget;
  - the decoder block at the 7B width.
- Against step 1's JSON, the bytes differ only inside the relocation
  fields, and the lines' ranges are the same.
- The code a run executes is unchanged: the same bytes, linked. X1's
  harness differs from the baseline in the same 19 files, by their version
  lines. `make test` passes, and the manual builds without a warning.

## D146 — Version 0.14.1 opened: the exploded view, by a compositional layout of the network diagram (2026-10-17)

The plan is `presk-specs/implementation/presk-plan-0.14.1.md` (presk-specs
!94, open). On the Network tab the user asked, on 2026-10-17, via the
paper session: "On devrait pouvoir déplier toutes les boîtes, pour
arriver à une vue éclatée complète du graphe, pas juste une boîte à la
fois." That is two asks:
- a fully exploded view, every box open and every stack at one layer;
- opening a box without folding its siblings. 0.14.0 step 1 departed
  from its plan there (D141's second departure), because its positions
  are precomputed per opening, one chain of boxes each, and an arbitrary
  set of open boxes would need 2ⁿ of them.

**The user's decision (2026-10-17, via the paper session): option C, a
compositional layout.**
- Each box's graph is laid out once, in its own frame, with its children
  folded.
- An opening composes the frames: an open box takes its composed size,
  the items after it in its layer move right by its growth, the layers
  below move down by their layer's growth, and nothing is reordered.
- The page composes any set of open boxes, and all of them: "expand all",
  "fold all", a header toggling its own box alone, and the lesson and the
  address recording the open set.
- The exporters compose by the same rule: `presk dump --stage network
  --level all`.

The alternatives the paper session set beside it were:
- (A) one more precomputed opening, "exploded", the siblings still
  folding;
- (B) the layered layout ported to JavaScript, with the Rust layout as
  its oracle.

**The form: version 0.14.1, not a merge after the tag.** Positions of
record move: the report's figure 9.1 (level 1), the manual's
`explain_network` figure (level 2) and `network.svg`. `explain.json`'s
format moves to 3, one frame per box replacing the views per opening.
Nothing else moves: the graph, its numbers, the table, `explain.md`.

**Facts checked** (a scratch test, not committed, on the course GPT's
`loss` at D = 64 in `f64`):
- *The layout is already compositional in its structure.*
  `layout::graph(b, open)` lays out the graph of `b` with each open child
  at its own graph's size. The layers and their order never depend on
  which boxes are open, only the coordinates do, so only the
  precomputation is per chain. A function laying out any set reproduces
  the 14 precomputed views exactly, rectangles and routes.
- *The exploded view* is 1 101 × 3 954 pt: 125 nodes, 13 boxes four
  levels deep, 133 arrows. On an A4 text block it would print at scale
  0.18, so it is for the page and the SVG.
- *The shift rule against today's.* A prototype of C gives the same
  overall sizes (level 1 647 × 899 pt, level 2 741 × 1 569, the exploded
  1 101 × 3 954). Inside, it moves 5 of the 24 rectangles at level 1 (at
  most 132 pt) and 21 of 38 at level 2 (at most 203 pt), mostly the nodes
  after an open box and the arrows, which today's rule re-centres.
  Side by side, the drawings are nearly the same.
- *What does not move:* the entry alone and every box drawn alone,
  figure 9.2 among them, since each is a single frame.
- *The JSON:* the `network` object is 121 KB on the course GPT under a
  budget, 36 KB of it for 14 views; 85 KB on the decoder block at the 7B
  width, 19 KB of it for 12 views.

**Statements, fixed before the work** (the plan's §3):
- **E0:** nothing else moves, against `2702f96`. `explain.json` changes
  only in its `format` and its positions.
- **E1:** the openings compose. A box with no child open is drawn as its
  frame, translated; the layers and their order are kept; no two
  siblings overlap; every child lies inside its box; every arrow meets an
  open box at its port. Checked in every chain opening, in the exploded
  one and in 20 random open sets on each of the 36 diagrams.
- **E2:** any open set in the page, and N1's clicks on the exploded view.
- **E3:** one rule. The page's positions equal the compiler's for the
  default and exploded openings, and the SVG and the TikZ draw the
  compiler's.
- **E4:** N1 to N4 still hold.
- **E5:** with everything open, the decoder block's page answers under
  P3's 200 ms.

E0's baseline: X1's harness on `2702f96`'s release build
(`out/bin/presk-2702f96`) into `out/x1/base-0.14.1`, with `make
quant-table`, `step-table` and `tutorial` beside it. Version `0.14.1-dev`.

**Done (2026-10-17).** Steps 0 to 3 on the branch `0.14.1`, one presk
merge request with presk-specs !94. What the version did:
